definition: the game of jumping over a raised bar or cord, and the bar itself; with <kan.4>, step over, as {kanteh kan}, do the high jump

terms: from one side/from another point of view/in another way
definition: <lamkhat> and <pan> written as one word: from one side; {lamkhatpan in genleng} is to put it another way
a table for eating, reading or setting things on; two articles add <sabuai> to explain it
sticky rice or sticky millet, steamed for feasts such as Khuado and for the visit to the graves; mostly spelled <taksih>, and {taksih nganhuan} is to steam it

terms: that he founded/which was set up
definition: <a> and <phuh> written as one word: that he founded or set up, said of a church, a village or a post
<a> and <huan.1>, garden, written as one word: his, her or their garden
<a> and <huan.3>, cook, written as one word: the one who cooks, or he or she cooks
<tui> and <nuai> written as one word: the place under the water; before a noun it means underwater, as in an underwater drone
<siangtho> and <pumpi> written as one word: the holy body of Jesus given in the Lord's Supper
<zong.5>, seek, and <lo> written as one word: not seek, without looking for
of two things, views or parties: be contrary to each other, go against each other, with <tawh> for the other side
<duang>, figure, with <cing.3>, be complete: having a fine, well-formed body, said with <melhoih> of good-looking women and men; {duangcing kidemna} is a contest of physique

terms: be short of/not have enough/be hard-pressed
definition: <kicing>, enough, with <lah>, here lacking: of money, goods or a person, fall short, not have enough for what is needed
of a person who acts as if never having enough: be greedy for a share, or push in where it is not one's place
<taam> and <ding> written as one word: will stay, in order to stay for a time
<a> and <beina> written as one word: the end of it, its coming to an end
<kaam>, luck, with <sinna>, a trying: a draw of numbered tickets sold to raise money, in which the winners get prizes
<lam>, road, with <khak>, shut: a roadblock where police or soldiers stop travellers, and anything that bars the way
hold something to be important or dear, give it the first place, said beside <thupisak>
reach over and take in the whole of something, as {leitung bup huap}, cover the whole world; said beside <huam>
placed after a verb of sinking, lessening, easing or growing dark: it happens bit by bit and keeps on

terms: out again and again/down one after another
definition: <khiat> said twice, after a verb or as the verb itself: the taking out or dropping is done again and again, one after another
the man of a village who deals with the <dawi>, the spirits, in the old religion, named together with the <siampu> or <siampi>, priest
<a> and <nun>, life, written as one word, the first part of {anun tak} and {anun takna}, his or her living, way of life, which is otherwise written with <nuntak> and <nuntakna>
<a> and <nun>, blow, written as one word, said of the wind or a storm
New York, the largest city of the United States, written as one word
moving pictures recorded and shown on a screen, a common spelling of the English word video
<khua>, village, and <tuam>, separate, written as one word: a village of its own, or a different village, as <gamtuam> is a different country
the people of the <Tawmging> clan, who held the chieftainship of Saizang
<minvawh>, give a name, with the noun suffix <na>: the name given to a people, a group or a thing, and the giving of it
a quarter, {Botung veng}, of the town of <Tedim>; the name is also found at Vangteh
<kikup> and <ding> written as one word: will talk a matter over together, something to be discussed
a thing that a smith forges of iron, wanted by young women and given as a gift; taken here as the pipe for smoking tobacco
<pak>, for a moment, and <leng>, if I or we, written as one word after a verb: if we do it briefly, used by writers to say let us briefly look at or mention something
<ka> and <phat> written as one word: I praise, I give thanks for
<i> and <sisan> written as one word: our blood, the common descent of a people
<nuam>, want, and <ten>, the plural with the marker of the doer, written as one word after a verb: those who want to do it, as the ones who act

terms: upper part of a village/above the village
definition: <khua>, village or town, and <tung>, above, written as one word: the upper side of a village or the place over a town; also part of village names such as Mualnuam Khuatung
<a> and <vaak> written as one word: go about from place to place, the one who goes about; in lists of caring for children or sheep it is <vaak> in its sense of feeding
<mai>, just, and <mah> written as one word after a verb at the end of a sentence, in writing from Manipur: it simply is so
<mai>, face, and <mah> written as one word: the face itself
placed after <bang>, like, or after a noun: exactly so, just the same, as {tua bang ngeiingeii in}, in just that way; after a verb, surely; it may be the same word as <ngeingei>

terms: those who will enter/those to go in
definition: <lutding> with the plural <te>: the people who are to go in, as to an interview
<hong> and <piakhia> written as one word: give out to us, donate to the speaker or his group
<na> and <piaknop> written as one word: you want to give, mostly before <leh>, if
<kamphen>, interpreter, with <pa> for a man: the man who interprets for a speaker
<mawng>, banyan, with <pi>, great: a large banyan tree; with a capital also the name of a hill and a name of persons
<det> said twice, after a verb: keeping on steadily, as tears that keep falling, or going into a matter thoroughly, as {ngaihsun detdet}, think it through, and {sui detdet}, examine closely
stir or push into action; {han thot na} is a word of exhortation at a meeting, and one writer explains the word as impact
<hong> and <bang> written as one word: come to be like something, or seem so to the speaker
<khan> in the sense of a room, as in <innkhan>, with <ah> written as one word: in the room, as {lupna khanah}, in the bedroom; not the word for lifetime
<sa>, meat, with <kal>, kidney: the kidney of an animal as meat, named with <salung> among the choice parts given to the elders
Astaka sports complex in Petaling Jaya, Malaysia, where the Zomi football tournaments are played
move a thing or oneself from its place, compare <kikhin>: {nung khiin} is draw back, {nawl khiin} is push aside or abolish, and {ki khiin} is be moved

terms: social skill/ability to get along with people
definition: <kikholh>, keep company with, and <siamna>, skill: being good at mixing and getting along with other people
<sem>, work or serve, spelled with a long vowel, and <ding> written as one word: will serve, to hold an office or do a work
<dawn>, drink, with the ending <pih>: drink together with someone, or give someone tea, beer or another drink as a host
<panpih>, help, and <theih>, be able, written as one word, the form of <panpihthei> used before <nading> and before a noun: that can be helped, so as to be able to help
<hel>, include, and <ding> written as one word, mostly after <ki>: will be included, will take part, to join in
<zom>, continue or join, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not going on with something, and after <ki> not joined to it
the village in the hill country, <khamtung>, that a person or family comes from, given in profiles of people who now live elsewhere
<lai>, writing, with <gelhdan>, way of writing: how a language is written and spelled
a village named as the home village of Zomi people and of a village association, {Chantagyi Khua Kipawlna}; the Burmese name suggests the plains of Myanmar
<a> and <kipuah> written as one word: that has been repaired, improved or put in order; {akipuah toto} is improved again and again
<nam>, people, with <phung>, clan: a tribe, a division of a people larger than a <beh>, clan, and smaller than the <minam>, nation; the articles gloss it with English tribe
the prefix <ki> and <semzo>, be able to do, written as one word: can be done, gets done

<taang>, millet, with <za>, hundred: a harvest of a hundred measures of millet, the mark of a wealthy household, named together with <mimza>; {taangza aih} is the traditional feast of the <Zomi> that celebrates it
the heavy metal used as fuel for nuclear power and in atomic bombs
the folder of an email account where incoming messages arrive
the English plural of <sponsor> used as a noun: the people who pay for an event, or the support they give, as in {sponsors hongpia teng}, those who gave sponsorship

terms: at the time of/in the days of/when
definition: <hunlai>, time or period, and <in> written as one word: at that time, in the days of the person or state named before; {tua hunlaiin} is at that time

<tuamtuam>, various, written as one word with <na>, thing, or with the noun ending {-na} of the word before it: various things, or the various ones of what the word before names, as in {kipawl natuamtuam}, the various organisations
<ngeilo>, never, and <ding> written as one word, after a verb: will never do or be so

terms: be free from/be exempt from/keep out of
definition: <peng>, be exempt, with the prefix <ki>: be clear of or stand apart from something, which is marked by <tawh>; {kipeng thei lo} is cannot be free of it or cannot stay out of it
the particle <hong>, spelled without its first letter, and <huh>, help, written as one word: help towards the speaker, help us or help me

terms: happen to be/there happen to be
definition: <a> and <omkhak>, happen to be, written as one word with a long vowel in the last syllable; {khialhna aomkhaak aleh} is if there should happen to be a mistake, a closing formula of news writers
<tun>, arrive, and <sawm>, intend, written as one word: make sure to be there, used in notices that tell people to come before a set hour
<thu>, word or matter, with <zasak>, make hear: let someone know a matter, report it to an office, or give notice or an order
<tuambawlna>, unequal treatment, with the prefix <ki>: people of one group treating one another as separate, forming sides and favouring their own
<zak>, hear, and <teh>, when, written as one word: when someone hears or heard it
<i>, our, and <pau>, language, written as one word: our language, said of the speech of the Zomi
a village or quarter at <Kalaymyo> in the plains of Myanmar where Zomi live; {Sanpya lampi} is Sanpya road
<an>, food, with the ending <pi>, main or great: the food a people mainly lives on, or the main dish of a meal
<bawl>, make, and <pawl>, group, written as one word after what is made: the group of people who make or carry it out, as in {thukhun bawlpawl}, the makers of the law
<bek>, only, and <ding> written as one word, after a verb: will only do or be that and nothing more
<tual>, the communal ground of a village, with <biak>, worship: the sacrifice of the old Zomi religion made by a whole village, the same as <tualbiakna>; {Tualbiak-pawi} is its festival
a bird of the hills whose call is heard through the dry season, also called {lawkta}
word of songs and formal wishes for what lies ahead of a person or a people, often paired with <masuan> as {masuan mazap}
Mount Popa, a volcanic mountain in central Myanmar near Bagan, named in accounts of where the Zomi once lived and also written {Pupa}
<loding> and the sentence-final <hi> written as one word after a verb: closes a statement that something will not happen
<cidamna> and <lam> written as one word: the side of health, matters of health and medicine
a place where books are kept for people to read, from <laibu>, book
<lungngaih> and <huai> written as one word: that calls for careful thought, that one ought to think over
the government of India or of one of its states, in the writing of Zomi in India; elsewhere <kumpi>
a woven container of the farming household in which goods and food such as taro are kept, named beside <lawhpi>; in a few sentences the same spelling stands for <lawhcing>, successful
<nam>, kind, and <sawm>, ten, written as one word after a noun: ten of them, ten kinds; {Thukham namsawm} is the Ten Commandments
in {sum dipkikna}, the payment by which the members of a mutual aid fund fill the fund up again after money has been paid out of it
<gam>, country, with <pawl>, group: a group or union of countries, as in {EU gampawl} and {NATO gampawl}
<bal>, taro, with <pi>, great: the taro plant and its large tuber, a common food crop of the Zomi hills, named beside {balke}
port city in the south of France, where the Zomi labour companies landed in 1917
the moon when it is full, and the day of the month on which it is full, {khaliik ni}; set against <khadet>, the new moon
<tui>, water, with <khuat>, dig: dig out the water source of a new village, said together with <khuasat>, found a village, of the first settlers
narrow in extent or in outlook, set against <zaii>, the same writer's spelling of <zai>, wide; {toii sa} is find something narrow
<na>, the marker of something done earlier or elsewhere, and <ciamteh> written as one word: has noted or recorded it, and after <in>, has regarded it as
<i>, we, and <tel>, understand, written as one word: we understand, we grasp

the land and villages on the far side as seen from where one stands, <gal>, other side, with <khua>: {galkhua dak} is look out over it, and in songs {galkhua don} is gaze toward the far land with longing
town in central Myanmar, now part of Naypyidaw, known for its agricultural college and university
<gen>, say, and <suk>, down, written as one word: go on to speak of what follows, or what has been said in the lines above
a person who represents a people, a party or an organization, above all an elected member of parliament, {Hluttaw kosale}; the Zolai words are <palai> and <taangmi>
noun of <kizem>: the adorning of oneself with clothes and ornaments, the decoration of a house or room, and the things used for it
<muh>, see, with <sawm>: form a picture of something before seeing it; {ka muhsawm dan sangin} is more than I had imagined
after <ki>, plan to see one another, arrange a meeting
noun of <ven>: the coming to an end of a war, a trouble or a dispute; {gal venna} is the end of a war and {buaina venna} the settling of a conflict
a heap or setting of stones raised as a memorial to a person, from <suang>, stone, and <phuh>, set up; also part of place names
expressive word placed after a verb or a describing word for something big and bulky that stands, lies or is held in plain view, as in {gol bembam}, great and bulky
word of songs for <kiangah>, to or beside a person: {na siangah} is to your side
<lung>, heart, and the place marker <ah> written as one word: in the heart or mind, mostly in songs

terms: at the time of/in the days of
definition: <hunlai> and <a> written as one word after a date, a name or a clause: in or of the time when that was so
{Kawl}, Burmese, with the Burmese word for country: Burma, as the land is named in one series of comic dialogues; the usual word is <Kawlgam>
<laih>, replace, with <to>, onward: one thing takes the place of another in turn, as a new model or name replaces the old; {laihsuk laihto} is change back and forth
<a> and <danin> written as one word: in the manner of what is named before it, as in {hih anuai adanin}, as shown below, and {abeisa adanin}, as in the past
<na> and <tup> written as one word: what you aim at or intend, often paired with {na ngimna} and {na sawmna}
placed after a verb: the action is all that is done or goes on being done, merely, single-mindedly, as in {buaipih lunglung}, be taken up with nothing else
<tum>, set, and <ta> written as one word: of the sun or of the days of a life, has now gone down, is coming to an end
<tum>, play an instrument, and <ta> written as one word: has come to play, began playing

terms: be rejected/be cast aside/reject one another
definition: <pampaih>, cast aside, with the prefix <ki>: be left aside as of no account, or reject one another; {kipampaih thei lo} is cannot be set aside
<la>, song, with <pu>: in {Zogam Lapu}, a title of honour given to a senior Zomi songwriter
<kipatcil>, first beginning, with the noun suffix <na>: the very beginning of something, or the place and time where it began
plural of <siampu>: the priests of the traditional religion; {zato siampute} are physicians
town in the south of the Manipur valley in India, near the hills where Zomi villages lie
<koici>, how, and <dan>, manner, written as one word: in what way, of what sort
<dot>, ask, and <behnop>, want to add, written as one word: wishing to ask something more; {dotbehnop a om leh} in a notice is if there is anything further to ask
<nop> and <dan>, manner, written as one word: after <a> how pleasant a place is, after a verb how much someone wants to do it, as in {ka theih nopdan}, how I long to know
<tut>, sit, and <khawl>, rest, written as one word: sit down for a rest, stop and sit; paired with <dinkhawl>, stand still
second part of the name Sierra Leone, a country in West Africa
<tawn>, follow a path, with <zia>, manner: the ways a people follows and hands down, as in {pupa tawnzia}, the customs of the forefathers; often beside <ngeina>
<hong> and <sung> as a verb, pour out, written as one word: set out a view or account before the readers, as in {ka muhna hongsung nuam-ing}, I wish to present my view; not the word for in
placed after a verb: in a big or showy way, as in {minpua lianluan}, bear a title grandly, and {kilam lianluan}, be built on a grand scale
city in the state of Missouri in the United States, in the news in 2014 for unrest after a police shooting; also an English surname
<min>, name, with <san>, from <saang>, receive: the taking down of names, said of refugees being registered by the UNHCR
short form of <khuaphelep>: electric power, mostly as {khuaphe mei}, electric light or supply, and {khuaphe meiset}, electric generator
a flash of lightning, compare <khuaphia>
<sa>, game, with {ben}, from <beng>, hunt: the hunting of wild animals; {saben in ben} is hunt down, said also of pursuing wanted men
<nawh>, hurry, with <tak>: in haste, as a matter of urgency
<bua>, pour out, and <sa> written as one word: already spilled; known from the proverb {tui buasa kiluak kik thei lo}, spilled water cannot be scooped up again
placed after a verb: the action goes on briskly and without letting up, as in {buai citcit}, be in a great stir, and of birds {ham citcit}, keep chirping
<tuisawp>, baptism, with the noun suffix <na>: the rite of baptism; {tuisawpna pia} is baptize and {tuisawpna ngah} is be baptized
a large bag carried on the back or shoulder for one's things on a journey or to the field, compare <thung-ip>
open footwear, slippers or sandals, as against closed shoes
placed after a noun: of every kind, as in {paak namcih}, all kinds of flowers; in songs also every people, all nations
words of power spoken by a priest or a man with such knowledge; mostly in {phui sam}, say an incantation, see <phuisam>; also said as an exclamation of scorn
only in {mat leh zet} and {kimat zet}: one following close on another without a break, as vehicles passing or people talking
<mi> and <gen> written as one word: what others say, people talking; {migen za} is hear people say
<dang>, throat, with <keu>, dry: be thirsty, or thirst; {dangkeu pha sak} is quench the thirst
<a> and <siahuai> written as one word: that which is bad or terrible; {asiahuai bangmah omlo} is there is nothing wrong
<akhak>, send, and <nuam>, want, written as one word: {akhaknuam te} are those who wish to send something
placed after a verb or noun: exactly so, in the strict sense, as in {kituak liinlian}, fit exactly, and {akibang liinlian}, exactly the same
<ih>, we, and <suak>, become, written as one word: we become, we turn out to be
a city on the Irrawaddy in Bago Region, Myanmar, formerly called Prome, and the seat of a Catholic diocese
<ih> and <pate> written as one word: our fathers, mostly in the pair {ihpu ihpate}, our forefathers

terms: those who base on/those who rely on
definition: those who make something their foundation or main concern, <bulphuh> with plural {-te}, after <a>
worth having or owning, <neih> with the ending {-huai}, worthy of
<ham.2> and <zaw> written as one word: older in age than another, with <sang> for than
<ngai.2> and <in> written as one word: missing or longing for a person or thing, said of what one does meanwhile
<hong> and <tu.2> written as one word: come and sit or settle at a place, land there, or of a duty come to rest on someone
strikingly fine or bright, said of dress, of a day and of a literature; {mei vam} is glowing embers
the man who found or discovered something, <mukhia> with the ending {-pa}
a principle or policy that a group holds and follows; {thulet bulpi} is a basic principle
<siam> and <dan> written as one word: the way or degree in which one is skilled at something
a dark-skinned foreigner, such as an Indian, mostly paired with {mangkang}, a white foreigner: {mangvom mangkang} is foreigners of every kind
<veng.2> and <nuai> written as one word: the lower quarter of a town or village, also used as the name of such a quarter
<khang> and <masate> written as one word: the people of earlier generations
plural of <Indian>; in the articles mostly the native peoples of America, also {Red Indiante}
<ciau> and <tui> written as one word: the water of a river, a word of songs
<na> and <nau> written as one word: your younger brother or sister, or your baby
bearing much seed or many offspring, said of plants, animals and people; also to multiply in this way

terms: all the good ones/the good part
definition: <hoih> and <teng.3> written as one word: all that is good of something, the good ones or the best part
<ngei> and <mah> written as one word: just as one is used to; {ngeimah bangin} is as usual, as before
<zangh> said twice: go on using something, use it again and again
found after <na> only: {na lengah} is <naleng> with <ah> divided in another place, even in, even at
<kiho> and <sak> written as one word: cause or allow people to talk with one another, put someone in touch with another
a village of the Khuangnung tract in the Tedim area
writing done by hand, or a text written by hand; {khutgelh lai} is a manuscript
<om> and <ciangin> written as one word: when someone is at a place or when something is there
after a verb, said of an action that goes on or is done again and again, as chatting or grumbling; {lu susu} is said of a sleepy person whose head keeps nodding
what makes a person, a people or a teaching different from all others
the muscles and sinews of the body, the seat of its strength; often paired with <thagui>
<gah> and <hoih> written as one word: good fruit, mostly of the good results of a way of life
dealings and traffic between people, villages or countries
<tawi> and <in> written as one word: holding or carrying something in the hand while doing something else
a bishop of the Roman Catholic Church, <siadaw> with the ending {-pi}, great
<i> and <phung.2> written as one word: our clan or family line, mostly in {i beh iphung}
stay on at a place or on the way longer than needed, be held up there
regard oneself as good at something or act as if one were, <kisiam> with <sak>
roll or tie several things into one, and of speech gather several points into one
<na> and <teel> written as one word: either you choose, or with the narrative <na> before the verb, chose or elected
<om>, <lo> and <hi> written as one word: there is not, it does not exist
<a> and <zote> written as one word: those who have finished or passed something, or those who won
the marker <in> written together with the prefix {ki-} of the verb that follows: {inki nei} is {in kinei}
in a firm and lasting way, often paired with <kiptak>
<zui> and <siam> written as one word: be good at following a leader, a rule or a custom

expressive word after a word for a colour or for light and dark: faintly, dimly so; {khuavak philhphelh} is the first faint light of dawn, {khuamial philhphelh} is dusk, and {puang philhphelh} is dull grey
the Houthis, an armed Shia movement of <Yemen> that fights the government of that country
<limci>, good, with <tak> written as one word: very good, excellent, said of an event or a result
a city in the state of <Iowa> in the United States, where a Zomi community lives
Fort Worth, a city in Texas in the United States near <Dallas>, written as one word
<na>, your, and <pasal>, husband, written as one word: your husband
<nuphal> with <pa> for a man: a man who is related to the speaker by marriage as nuphal, by the lexicon the husband of the sister of the wife; the sentences do not show the exact relation
the low, hot country along the rivers and to the south, where crops ripen early, as against <Zogam>, the cool high country
<hong> and <leng>, fly, written as one word: come flying, fly this way, of a bird, a swarm or an aeroplane and its passengers; {lung hongleng} is come to feel lonely
<kum>, year, with <sum>, money: money paid once a year, as the yearly dues of a member or the yearly fee for a service
in {kumsum hun}, the year of the budget of a government, the financial year
steps or a ladder for going up and down, as against a lift
<lo>, not, and <zawin> written as one word, mostly as {hi lozawin}: it is not that, but rather what follows

terms: merely/only as far as/no more than
definition: <ciang>, as far as, and <lel>, only, written as one word after a noun phrase: no further than that, merely that
expressive word after a verb for something done lightly and again and again: of rain, drizzling, as {guah zu supsup}; of people, talking low among themselves, as {kiho supsup}
tell someone plainly that he is wrong in order to set him right; named together with <hilh>, teach
a district of the city of <Seremban> in Malaysia
<i>, we, and <kalsuan>, step, written as one word: we go forward, our going forward
<sum>, money, with <nu>, mother: used in the pair {sumnu sumpa}, money of every kind, wealth, as something sought, earned or asked for in a blessing
<sum>, money, with <pa>, father: the second half of the pair {sumnu sumpa}, money of every kind, wealth; see <sumnu>
<hong> and <zuan>, head for, written as one word: come heading for a place or a person
<khuapih> and <tuipih> written as one word: the people of the same town or village, named after the relatives and acquaintances of a person
<zu>, liquor, and <zuak>, sell, written as one word: sell liquor, the selling of liquor; {zuzuak na} is a place where liquor is sold and {zuzuak nu} is a woman who sells it
expressive word after a word for smiling or for warmth: {nui hieuhiau} is smile softly and {lum hieuhiau} is mildly warm; perhaps the same word as <hiauhiau>
<manpha>, valuable, with <tak> written as one word: very valuable; {manphatak in} is in a way that has worth, to good purpose
poetic word of songs, made of a song word for mother and <sung>, inside; used in {tunsung khat pan piang}, born of one womb, said of the Zomi as one family
<Zotual>, native Zo, and <lai>, writing, written as one word: the native Zo script of Pau Cin Hau, also called {Laipian lai}
<ki> with <phual>, camp: have one's base or home in a place, said of a people, a church body or an armed group
<thei>, can, and the linking <a> written as one word: it can be so, and
<kipawlkhawm>, unite, and <in> written as one word: joining together, as one body
<gam>, land, with <nei>, have: one who owns land or to whom a territory belongs; before a noun, land-owning; of a people, having a land of its own
<kong>, I to you, and <sam>, invite, written as one word: I or we invite you, the closing words of an invitation
<suaktatak>, freely, and <in> written as one word: freely, without hindrance

a city in <Ohio>, United States

old village of the Sihzang people near Pimpih in the Tedim area

the time of youth when a person is in bloom and at full strength, a word of songs and poems
<zin> and <lai> written as one word: the time when someone is travelling or visiting a place, while on a journey

what is in regular or everyday use, and so also a habit that someone keeps; from <zattang>, common use, and <zang>, use

terms: to be able to read/so that it can be read
definition: <simtheih> and <ding> written as one word: for someone to be able to read, mostly as {simtheihding in}, so that it can be read
the living of a teaching or word in one's own life, putting it into practice, set against only saying it
<la>, song, and <tawh>, with, written as one word: with or by a song; {latawh kisai} is concerning songs

<neih>, have, and <teh>, when, written as one word: when one has; {hun neihteh} is when there is time
<na>, you, and <nget>, ask for, written as one word: you ask for or apply for; {thu nanget} is you pray

terms: be fond of/cherish/be loath to leave
definition: be so attached to a person, place or thing that one is unwilling to part with it; {khiatlah huai} is dear, hard to leave
<vaihawm> and <pawl> written as one word: the group that manages or decides the affairs of an organisation, a committee or management team
<hunlap> and <in> written as one word, mostly as {a hunlapin}: in time, at the proper time

terms: pray for you/ask on your behalf
definition: <kong> and <ngetsak> written as one word: I or we pray for you, mostly as {thu kongngetsak hi} at the end of a message of sympathy or thanks
the passing of news between people, communication; {nisim thukizaakna} is a newspaper

placed after a verb: although that is so, granted that, before a clause that says something in spite of it
<tung> and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word: arrived, reached, came upon
<ado> and <ding> written as one word: to fight against, that which is to be fought; {adoding in} is in order to fight
make things the same as one another, bring into one form, as spelling, speech or opinions
<ihmu> and <lo> written as one word: not sleep, without sleeping; {ihmulo liangin} is going even without sleep
the state of being free, and the freedoms a person is entitled to: {mihing zaleenna} is human rights; given beside <suahtakna>

<kong> and <pai> written as one word: I come to you, I have come here
<a> and <dung> written as one word: its length, the long side, paired with <avai> or {a vai}, its width

<tu>, grandchild, <leh>, and, and <tate>, children, written as one word: the generations that come after, descendants

<gel>, plan, with <khawm>, together, written as one word: think out and decide a matter jointly

<ka>, I, and <ko>, express, written as one word after <lungdam> or <lungdamna>: I or we express thanks

the particle <na> and <kigelh> written as one word: it is found written, it stands written, said of a text that is quoted

<neu> and <nono> written as one word: small, said of several things that are each small

in writing about Buddhism, the teaching of a Buddha and the age in which it lasts

<cin> and <lo> written as one word: not reaching the full amount, not enough for the need, not up to what is required

<phi> and <dingte> written as one word: those who are going to sit an interview or a test

<van>, sky, with <khawh>, stab: piercing the sky, said of a very tall building; {vankhawh inn} is a skyscraper

what is done for pleasure, amusement or a social celebration
<len>, hold, with <suak>, on: go on holding an office, a post or power

<lam>, dance, with <tual>, open space: the ground where the village dances

<lei>, buy, and the linking <in> written as one word: buying, having bought, before the verb that follows

descriptive word placed after a verb for something that dribbles, is smeared or lies about in a mess, often followed by <den>

<kikheek> with the noun ending {-na}: an exchanging between two sides, as {thautang kikheekna}, an exchange of fire; also a change of place or post
<la>, take, and the particle <ta> written as one word: has now taken, or with <ding> is now to be taken; {kiciamna lata} is has taken the oath

terms: serve as a dish/give to eat with
definition: give someone a food as <meh>, the dish that goes with the meal, or prepare it for them

terms: look around at one another/look about
definition: <ki> and <khuadak> written as one word: look around, at one another or in wonder and uncertainty
<tom> and <gen> written as one word: say in few words; {tomgen leng} is to put it briefly
<kham>, drunk, said twice, after <zu> or <zuu>, strong drink: get drunk again and again; a few sentences have it after <khen>, divide, of splitting again and again
<zun>, tend, said twice and paired with <puahpuah>: go on tending a language, a people or a land and putting it in order
the particle <hong>, spelled without its first letter, and <zin>, travel, written as one word: come here on a visit or journey
<hawl> said twice: go on driving a vehicle, or keep driving a person or an animal away
<i> and <pianna> written as one word: our birth or origin; {ipianna nu le pa} is the parents who gave us birth

terms: eat with/share a meal with/dine with
definition: <an>, food, and <nekpih> written as one word: eat a meal together with someone, take someone to a meal
<pate>, fathers, and the marker <in> of the doer written as one word, seen in {nu le patein}, the parents as the ones who act
<ki> and <tawldam> written as one word: one gets rest or relief from tiredness or strain
<lo>, field, and <hoih>, good, written as one word, mostly in the pair {innhoih lohoih}, a fine house and good fields, said of property and wealth
<meileng>, train, with the plural <te>
<ngen>, ask for, and the linking <a> written as one word: asking for something and then; {khutdawh ngena} is by begging
placed after a verb such as <pau>, speak, or <ci>, say: doing it carelessly or to no purpose, just going on doing it
a supporter of <Zomism>, the movement for the name and unity of the <Zomi>; a coinage on the English pattern used in political essays
<sahang>, tiger or wild beast, with <no>, young: the cub of a tiger
a substance in food that protects the cells of the body from damage
<phawk>, remember, with <pha>, reach: bring something fully to mind, be well aware of it
descriptive word placed after a word such as <neu>, small, <niam>, low, or <tol>, bald, picturing a thing as very small, shrunken or bare
poetic word for <gal>, enemy, used in songs; one article glosses it as {i galte}, our enemies
a means of crossing a river where there is no bridge, on which people are carried and hauled across; a dictionary has {khau kawn} for a hank of rope
<zaang>, plain or flat ground, and <ah>, at or on, written as one word: on the plain, on a flat place such as a flat roof
<na> and <ngai>, listen, written as one word: you listen, in a command {nangai un}, listen; also with the particle <na> of an action going on at that place or time, was listening
having a big belly; from <gil>, belly
<unau>, siblings, with the noun ending {-na}: being brothers, mostly as {ki unauna}, brotherhood among people
<a> and <vaaihawm> written as one word: he plans or arranges, the one who plans, what is planned
<a> and <kantel> written as one word: he or they investigate, the one who inquires into a matter thoroughly
<a> and <kullo> written as one word, placed after a verb: there is no need to do it, that which need not be done
the Tedim name of Rih Dil, a natural lake west of Tedim by the Tiau river on the border of Chin State and Mizoram, called {Lih bual} or {Lih Dil}

terms: I am good at/I know how
definition: <ka>, I, and <siam>, skilled, written as one word: I am good at it, I know it well; {kasiam tawp in} is as best I can
<om>, be, and <toto>, more and more, written as one word: there goes on being more of it, it keeps happening

<lel>, merely, and <lo> written as one word after a verb, before <ding> or in a question: it would simply be so, would it not; in one sentence it may instead be <lel>, be defeated, with <lo>, not give way
the pool at Tedim from whose glittering water the town is said to have its name; also called {Tuidim}
<Saizang> with the plural <te>: the people of Saizang and the group that speaks the Saizang dialect
a village named in the early history of the Tedim area
<vai>, matter, and <lianpi>, great, written as one word: a very weighty affair of a people or community
a kind of pot or jar, named among the pots for rice beer, {zu beeltung}; its size and shape are not settled
in news of war, a bomb dropped from the air, with <khia>, drop
<lunglut>, be interested, and <lo>, not, written as one word
<hong> and <theih>, the form of <thei>, know, written as one word: come to know, or know us; <hong> shows that the action comes toward the speaker
<ciamteh>, note, with <huai>, worthy of: worth noting or remembering

terms: in order to be able/so as to manage
definition: <zawh>, be able, and <nang>, short for <nading>, written as one word after a verb: so that it can be done

terms: want to attend/want to go to
definition: <kah>, attend, and <nuam>, want, written as one word: wish to attend a school; {President kahnuam} is one who wants to run for president
<se> and <hi> written as one word at the end of a statement, giving it emphasis: indeed, really
<hel>, mix, with <zau>, spread wide: mix different things or people together, mix one matter up with another
<ciim>, sensible or clear, with the comparative <zaw>: wiser, of the mind clearer and sharper
<thumuh>, insight, with <siamna>, skill: the ability to see into matters and understand them
<kamtuam>, a strange tongue, with <pau>, speak: speaking in tongues in church, also speech in a language the hearer does not understand
<taimang>, run away, with <pa>, man: the one who ran away; {tapa taimangpa} is the prodigal son of the parable
<a> and <kaal> written as one word: the week, as in {akaal nihna}, the second week, or with {-ah} the time or space in between
according to law, official, also the field of law; a form built on <upadi>, law, in the writing of one author who glosses it official
<ziau>, lightly or at once, and <lo>, not, written as one word after a verb: the action is not done simply, quickly or easily
<sawm>, ten, and <val>, exceed, written as one word: ten or more, some tens
<a> and <kiciam> written as one word: who vowed or promised, what was agreed, as in {akiciam ni}, the day agreed on
<i>, our, and <mai>, the front or the time ahead, written as one word: before us, our future, mostly with <lam>
<phuah>, give a name, and <zia>, way, written as one word: the way names are made up and given, used after <min>, name
<niam>, low, and <lua>, too much, written as one word: too low in place, level or standing
<taam>, stay, and <suak>, right through, written as one word: stay on in a place for good instead of going back
<sang>, school, and <huang>, enclosure, written as one word: the grounds of a school or university
take something without the owner knowing, quietly take out or steal; <la>, take, with <sim>, here secretly
<et>, look at, and <khak>, happen to, written as one word: come to look at or watch something, with or without meaning to
placed after a verb: the action is kept up steadily and without turning aside, as {en tengtang}, look fixedly
<sin>, learn, and <pah>, at once, written as one word: set about learning something straight away

terms: make compete/hold a contest/set against each other
definition: <kidem>, compete, with the causative <sak>, written as one word: have people or things compete for something
<ngah>, get, and <phet>, just, written as one word and followed by <in>: the moment something is received or caught
of a sight, drawing the eye and pleasant to look at; <mit>, eye, with <tai>, run
a clan or people that is small, short of members or not fully grown as a people, set against {namzau}, a widespread one; known from the old saying {namtom hauh leh tuita khan}

found only in {tuita khan}, growth that shoots up fast and does not last because it has no firm base, as in the old saying {namtom hauh leh tuita khan}; what the word names by itself is not clear from the articles

of termites, bite a way open through the ground; in the saying {phulum phul nading leikha in petlet}, the termites bite the way open for the winged termites to swarm out, said of those who prepare the way for others
<zawl>, sweetheart, with <hel>, court: the evening visits of a young man to a girl he seeks to win, the old custom of courting
<kimang>, be of use, and <thei>, able, written as one word: that can be used, that can be said of something, or that keeps and lasts
<ka>, my, and <cihnopna>, meaning, written as one word: what I mean to say
a blow on the cheek with the open hand, also the act of slapping someone; <pang>, here the cheek, with <bet>, slap
<tup>, aim, <leh>, and, <ngiim>, intend, written as one word: the aims and intentions of a person or an organisation
<mai>, just or simply, and <lo>, not, written as one word after a verb and before <dia> or {ding hiam}: a guess that expects agreement, will it not just be so
<mee>, vote, with the counting word <tang>, written as one word: a single vote, the votes cast for someone
<a> and <moi>, young, written as one word: young, the young one; {amoi pen} is the youngest and {amoi aham} young and old

terms: want too much/be too eager/long for
definition: <ut>, want, and <lua>, too much or very, written as one word: want something very much or too much
<kisin>, practise, and <khol>, beforehand, written as one word: practise or train ahead of the time of need
<lungkim>, be pleased, with the comparative <zaw>, written as one word: be more pleased or more satisfied
<sial>, the mithun, with <lu>, head: the head or skull of a mithun killed at a feast, kept in the house as a sign of the feasts given under the old religion
word of song language for <lutang>, the head; in prose once also the principal of a sum of money
at a later and unhurried time, by and by; once also gently, of a light blow; compare <damdam>, slowly
<midang> and the marker <in> written as one word: another person or other people as the one who acts

terms: go one's own way/stand apart/be divided
definition: keep apart from the others and act on one's own instead of working together, said of people and leaders who split a group; {mi-tangpeek} is used as a reproach for such a person
<thubaih>, an easy matter, and <lo>, not, written as one word: it is no easy matter, hard to do
<sa>, game, and <kap>, shoot, written as one word: shoot wild animals, hunt with a gun; also the one who shoots the animal
town and sub-division in the <Champhai> district of <Mizoram>, India
poetic word for a song that is sung, used in songs and song titles, mostly with <awi>, sing, as {zaideih awi}
of <Nigeria>, a person of Nigeria; the English word, used before words such as <gammi>, citizen
after a verb, of something white or bright that stands out clearly to the eye: {kang viuviau} is gleaming white
<zangsiam>, use well, with the plural <te>: those who make good use of a thing, of time or of a skill
<thuhilh>, teach, and <khial>, wrongly, written as one word: teach what is false; before {syate}, teachers, it describes false teachers
make something narrow or small in its reach, said of the mind, of a view and of the scope of a work; set against <liansak>, make large
<angsung>, one's own good, and <thei>, know, written as one word: knowing only one's own interest, selfish; also a selfish person
a stream on the road to <Tuizang> village in the Tedim area, crossed by a bridge; written small, {tuikai} is also said of a water tap
one single piece of something, as one strand of hair; with <zong> and a negative it means not even one, nothing at all

<zom>, continue or join, with the plural <te>: those who come next or carry on, and those joined to one another, as {laigui zomte}, kin of one navel cord; with a capital some writers use it for <Zomite>
literary word for people who are not one's own, other peoples; {siingdang eng lo} is envying no others
<i>, our, and <sepna>, work, written as one word: the work that we do
<ann>, food, and <lim>, tasty, written as one word: food that tastes good, a fine meal
show fondness to one another by touch, play and teasing, said of lovers and spouses and also of friends who are at ease with each other
one of the traditional kinds of Zo song with its own tune, named in lists beside <latung> and <zawlla>
<tun>, arrive, and <ciil>, first, written as one word: the time when one first arrives; {ka tunciil} is when I first arrived
<tualthat>, murder, with <pa> marking a man: the man who has killed someone
<Khazih>, Christ, and <mite>, people, written as one word: the people of Christ, Christians
poetic word for <gamsa>, wild animals that are hunted, used in songs
<kiteh>, be measured, and <lo>, not, written as one word: with <tawh>, is not measured or judged by something
in {inn lusi}, house by house, every household of a village; with a capital, Lusi is also a spelling of <Lusei>, the Lushai
the stretch of wild land and its cover where game is driven in a communal hunt; {sataang hawl} is drive the game from it and {sataang hal} is burn it
<um>, gourd, dried and cut as a ladle or bowl for scooping and serving soup and water
<don> said twice, mostly as {gal dondon}: keep looking out from afar for someone who is to come, wait for with longing
<thatang>, bodily strength, with the plural <te>: the strength and energy people have to give
a country in the south-east of <Africa>
stop what one is doing or stop on the way in order to rest; {khawlnga lo} is without a break
<manlang>, quick, with <sak>, make: make something go or happen faster
the hornbill, <phualva>, named as the bird of the Zo country; it mates for life and is the emblem of the Zomi, standing for love and faithfulness

terms: will not come/will not go/will not flow
definition: <pai>, go or come, and <loding>, will not, written as one word; {tui pailoding} is the water will not run
town in <Selangor>, <Malaysia>, known for its immigration detention camp, {Semunyih Camp}, where refugees were held
<vak>, go about, and the negative <loh> written as one word: not going out or about
<i>, our, and <maban> written as one word: what lies ahead of us, the rest of our course
form of <kivua>, <vuak> with the prefix <ki>: hit one another or be hit; also used as a noun, a beating
<thupibawl> with the prefix <ki>: be treated as important, or treat one another as important
<nungtolh> with the noun suffix {-na}: a going backward, the decline of a country or a falling back in faith
placed after a verb: holding to what one has said or wants and not giving way
descriptive word placed after a verb of speaking or doing: the action goes on easily and without pause, as in {phun siausiau}, keep grumbling
<an>, food, and <bang>, like, written as one word; in songs and poetic style {anbang it} is to love as one loves food, dearly
the particle <na> and <tai>, run, written as one word: ran or was running, said of someone other than the hearer
word of songs and elevated style, used as {holung kum} and before <kikum>: {holung kum} is talk a matter over, take counsel together

terms: worth keeping/to be kept/to be guarded
definition: <kep>, keep, with <huai>, worthy of: that should be kept and looked after
<khangto> with the noun suffix {-na}: the progress or development of a country or people
<ka>, I, and <kan>, ask or look into, written as one word
word of songs and poetic style for <gamla>, far; {gam vangla} is a distant land

terms: manage in full/be fully able/be fully content
definition: <kim>, all or fully, with <zo>, be able, written as one word: manage to do something in full or for everyone; {lung a kimzo} is the heart is fully content
<et>, look at, with <khialh>, wrongly, and the noun suffix {-na}: seeing a person or matter wrongly, and the ill feeling between people that comes of it; as {ki-etkhialhna} it is mutual
the particle <hong> and <en>, look, written as one word: look toward the speaker, or come and look
<i>, our, and <lawmte>, friends, written as one word; also said of the peoples around one's own, our peers
<kipawlna> with <pi>, great: a large or chief organisation, as the United Nations
a Zomi clan of the Tedim area, found among others at Khuasak, whose name is also borne as a surname
the fastener with two rows of teeth that opens and closes clothes and bags; {sik zit} is a metal zip
written where <zin>, travel, is expected, after <khual> or the name of a country: go on a journey

terms: be seen at once/be noticed right away
definition: <kimu>, be seen, with <pah>, at once, written as one word
<gam>, land, with <kip>, firm: a land or territory that a people or a village holds securely as its own
<khang>, generation, and <tampi>, many, written as one word
<zato> and <lam> written as one word: to the hospital, as in {zatolam kipuak}, be taken to hospital, or the field of medicine
a worker of the lowest rank in a government office or other body, who keeps watch and runs errands
<zek> with the emphatic <mah> written as one word, after a describing word or a word of time: to a fair degree; {nungkum zekmah in} is only last year or so
<mangngilh>, forget, with the causative <sak>: cause someone to forget
village in Mizoram, India, near the border with Chin State, where Zomi live
<phut>, set up, with the plural <te> written as one word: those who founded a church or an organisation
<pau>, language, and the marker <in> written as one word: in or by means of a language
<lungnuam>, be glad, and <pen>, most, written as one word
what a person or a meeting decides; {thupukna bawl} is make a decision or pass a resolution
<a> and <khangcing> written as one word: one that is mature or fully developed, or it grows to maturity
descriptive word placed after a verb of moving or sounding: the action goes on steadily or in a body, as people streaming toward a place; probably the word <nainai>
<ne>, eat, and <khin>, already, written as one word: have already eaten, eat something up
<zong>, also, and <tawh>, with, written as one word: with this one as well, even with
<siam>, skilled, with <tuam>, apart: skilled beyond others, and as a noun a special skill or a person who has one
<gamuk>, government, and <pawl>, group, written as one word: the body of those who govern a country or a state
<ni>, day, and <ta> written as one word after a date or the name of a day: that day, the day of

terms: hundred baskets of millet/great millet harvest
definition: a harvest of a hundred baskets of <mim>, millet, for which a man holds a feast of honour, named together with <taangza>
<a> and <lunggulhna> written as one word: his, her or their longing, what they wish for
<thu>, news, with <kizaksak>, inform one another, and the noun ending {-na}: the making known of news, an announcement, also a paper or record that carries it
<lamsang>, raise up, and <in> written as one word: lifting up, raising to a higher standing
<lam>, side or way, and <sangin>, than, written as one word: more than in the matter of, rather than in the way of
<ngah>, get, and <huai> written as one word: such that one gets something from it, {tha ngahhuai} is strengthening, {thupha ngahhuai} is a source of blessing
Sadar Hills, a hill area of Manipur in India
<sik>, step on, and <khak>, happen to, written as one word: happen to step on something, the form of <sikkha> used before <ding>
<kiim>, around, and <vial>, encircle, written as one word: go all the way round a place, or running all round it
the front of the leg between the knee and the ankle, {ngaltaak guh} is the shin bone; compare <ngaltak>
used in the pair {lamdung lamvai}, along the roads and byways, wherever one happens to be going
<thu>, news, and <zaksak>, make known, written as one word: tell people a piece of news, announce
<koi>, where, and <lak> written as one word, mostly with <ah>: where on earth, in a question or exclamation that expects the answer nowhere
<ba>, owe, with the prefix {ki-}: be in debt to someone, and of a sum, be still owed; {lei kiba} is owe a debt
used in the pair {nisa khasa}, the heat of sun and moon: the burning heat a person is exposed to out of doors
<neih>, have, and <kim>, every, written as one word: every one of them has it, have in every place
<ih>, we, and <dah>, grieve, written as one word: we are sad, we mourn
a state in the west of India
<kisak>, get ready, and <kholhna>, doing in advance, written as one word: getting ready beforehand
<meh>, the dish eaten with rice, with <kuang>, bowl: the bowl that curry or stew is served in, also a bowlful of it
know a person or thing by its marks, take note of it as such; one book of words explains <sansaat>, estimate, with it
come to have the mind of an owner of the house, be as much at ease as in one's own home; of a people or a faith, become settled in a place
noun of {kithuzaaktuah}, let one another hear news, compare <kithuzak>: communication among people by paper, radio or internet, and the information passed on
<ding> and <sang>, than, written as one word after a verb: rather than doing it, instead of doing it
<pi>, <leh> and <pu> written as one word: grandmother and grandfather, and so the forefathers
<lei>, buy, and <nuamte>, those who want, written as one word: the people who wish to buy something
<muh>, see, and <thak>, new, written as one word: something newly seen or found out
Saint Helena, an island in the South Atlantic Ocean
a state in the east of India, now named Odisha; in lists also its people
<phuh> and <ding> written as one word: to found or set up a church, an organisation or a country, what is to be founded
placed after a verb of what a group does: pictures many people doing it together and without stopping, as {nek khawm zaihzaih}, eating together
<zaih>, photograph, said twice, after <man> or <maan>, picture: take one photograph after another
<makaihsiam>, lead well, with the noun ending {-na}: the ability to lead people well
<hong>, here marking us as the object, and <uk>, rule, written as one word: rule over us, the one who rules us
<tan>, school class, with <nih>, two, written as one word: the second class of primary school, and the school reader of that class, above <tankhat>

terms: neighbour below/lower side of the house
definition: the house or people on the lower side of one's own, and the ground below the house; {innsak innkhang} together are the neighbours on every side
<ka> and <kap>, weep, written as one word: I weep, I cried
<ka> and <kap>, shoot, written as one word: I shoot, and with <uh> we shoot, in reports of fighting
descriptive word after a verb, mostly as {niang nuang}: in a slack, drooping or listless way
<pawl>, group, and <tuamtuam>, various, written as one word: the various groups, parties or denominations
<kizaksak>, inform one another, with the noun ending {-na}: the making known of news, an announcement, mostly as {thu kizaksakna}
<nau>, younger sibling, with <sung>, written as one word and used after {usung} or {u sung}: {usung nausung} is among elder and younger siblings, the circle of brothers, sisters and near kin
placed after a verb of sitting, staying or eating, often after <khawm>: of several people gathered close together in one place; near in use to <liailiai>, of which it may be a spelling
<a> and <sumh>, suffer loss, written as one word: the one who loses, what is lost
the English grammar term used in Zolai writing about language: a word of doing or being
<nungsang> with <in> written as one word, placed at the end of a clause, often after <khit>, or after a year: after, now that
<thuzuih>, following a teaching, with the noun ending {-na}: obedience, and the practice of a faith as distinct from its belief, <upna>
<naupang>, child, and <teng>, all, written as one word: all the children, the whole group of children or pupils
<ci>, say, and <kawm>, while, written as one word and mostly followed by <in>: while saying this, saying so and at the same time doing something else
<thuhilh>, preach, with {sya}, teacher, and the plural <te>, written as one word: those who preach and teach in the churches

terms: be planned for/be arranged for/be provided
definition: passive of <gelsak>, plan for someone, with the prefix {ki-}: be planned or arranged for someone, often after <hong> or <ong>, for us or for you
<kha>, moon, and <vak>, light, written as one word: the light of the moon, a night when the moon shines
<khuang>, crow, said twice: of roosters, crow repeatedly, as at daybreak; in songs a sign that it is time to wake
descriptive word after a verb or describing word such as <zam> or <gawng>: of a body, a neck, limbs or a tree that looks long, thin and stretched out
<a> and <thuap>, layer or patch, written as one word: what is laid on top of another; said twice, {athuap athuap}, layer upon layer, wave after wave
a village of Myanmar, given in news reports as the home village of Zomi people
of wood, smooth to the touch, rubbed or planed smooth, as {nawt ngil}, rub smooth
Lenggeng in Malaysia, site of an immigration detention camp, {Lengeng Camp}, named in reports about Zomi refugees
the noun ending {-na} and <ah> written as one word apart from the verb: in or at the doing of it, as {laivuan naah}, in the examinations; usually written {-na ah} or {-nah}
go right through something, as rays through cloth or the body; also see through a thing, after <muh>, and go beyond or past someone
the emphatic <vet> said twice with <lo>, not, written as one word: placed after a verb, not in the least, and after <ngei>, never once; stronger than <vetlo>
<kim>, every, and <phial>, almost, written as one word: placed after a noun or verb, nearly all of them, almost everywhere or in full
<deih>, want, and the particle <ta> of a change that has come, written as one word: now want, have come to want; {deih in deihta kei leh} is whether one wants it or not
<na>, your, and <zun>, urine, written as one word: in the old words for driving out a spirit, {nazun namsia}, your urine stinks
the particle <na> of an earlier action and <zun>, tend, written as one word: tended and built up in former times, paired with <puah>
<hibang>, like this, with the plural <te>, written as one word: things or people of this kind
<kisia>, be ruined, with the plural <te>, written as one word: the houses, bridges or towns that have been damaged; after <tawh>, those who have fallen out with someone
a number of things or beings gathered into one mass, as a heap of stones, a cluster of illnesses or a host of soldiers
<kik>, again, and <teh>, when, written as one word after a verb: when it is done again, as {ngaihsut kikteh}, when one thinks it over again
<kham>, be satisfied, and <tak> written as one word: eating or drinking as much as one wants
<nei>, have, and <khollo>, not much, written as one word: have little or none of something, or go without having arranged it

<khat>, one, and <lo>, not, written as one word after a noun: not of one and the same place or direction, so apart or different; {heina khatlo} is a phrase of songs for people who have gone separate ways
<angtang>, be proud, with <sak>, cause: make someone proud of what he or she is; {ki-angtangsak} is feel proud of oneself
<a> and <kilahna> written as one word: where someone was examined, of a clinic or hospital; also that by which something is shown

terms: compete with one another/vie/try to outdo
definition: <kidem>, compete, with <bawl>: keep trying to outdo one another, as in buying things or in getting ahead on the road
<kitawp>, resign, with the noun suffix {-na}: the act of leaving a post or office
<kitawp>, kiss one another, with the noun suffix {-na}: kissing
English exam with the noun suffix {-na}: an examination at school or university, also the testing of blood
<silh>, wear, and <loh>, not, written as one word, mostly before <ding>: not putting on a garment
<giak>, spend the night, and <suak>, on, written as one word: stay on and sleep at the place one has come to
