carry or send someone or something straight on to a place, as a patient to hospital, <puak> with <suak>
<dawp> and <nop> written as one word: wish to contact or inquire of an office or person
<sam> and <den> written as one word: call or invite again and again, always
<manlang> with the ending {-a}, mostly as {a manlanga}: quickly, as soon as possible
<an>, <leh> and <tui> written as one word: food and water, what one eats and drinks
the flowering and dying of the bamboo over a whole region, which comes after many years and brings swarms of rats and then famine; {mautam kialpi} is the famine that follows
<tuah>, meet with, and <teh>, when, written as one word: when one meets with trouble or the like
<kia> and <kik> written as one word: fall again, or fall back to a lower level, said of rain, prices and people
<hong> and <piankhiatna> written as one word: how something came into being, its origin
passive of <kankan>: be searched into or examined again and again, still be under investigation
put something or someone more into what is already there, as further members into a body or further words into a text
a person of China, or the Chinese as a people
plural of <zawhna>: the things someone has managed to do
water that wells up from the ground; in songs also a picture of what is sweet or flows freely
<khap> and <khat> written as one word: one span; {gilpi khapkhat}, the belly one span wide, stands for one's daily bread

terms: be entrusted with/be put in charge of/be given to hold
definition: passive of <lensak>: be given something to hold or handle, or be put in a post
the great examination at the end of a school or university year, above all the tenth standard examination, <laihuan> with <pi>
make something bigger or more important than it is, <uang> with <sak>
<sa> and <bang> written as one word in songs: like the wild animals, said of people who roam or live together, as in {sabang tat}
<thei>, can, and <ziau> written as one word after a verb: be able to do it readily, at once
the visiting of young women by young men in the evening, and the place or occasion of it
<a> and <kiniam> written as one word, in the sentences always as {akiniam khiat}: who humbles himself, who takes the lower place
<heh> and <pah> written as one word: become angry straight away

terms: be able to give/manage to give
definition: <apia> and <zo>, be able to, written as one word: the one who is able to give, he manages to give

terms: let us try to/let us aim to
definition: <sawm>, intend, and <ni>, let us, written as one word after a verb: let us set out to do it
<acih> and <ding> written as one word: that he should say or call something so
<gam> and <bang>, like, written as one word after the name of a country: a country such as the one named
<koh> said twice and written as one word: express or bring something up again and again, with <lungdam> keep giving thanks
<kizaih> with the plural <te>: the pictures or videos that were taken
used before <cing>, be full, mostly in songs and elevated language, of wishes and aims that are all fulfilled; apparently a word for a deep pool with <bang>, like: full as a pool
<pholak>, reveal, with the noun ending {-na}: the bringing of something into the open
the water of a salt or mineral spring, the first part being the old word for such a spring and not the verb die; the spring at Saizang is given as the origin of the name <Sihzang>
<a> and <khanna> written as one word: his, her or their growing up, or the growth of something
<kual>, area, and <teng>, all, written as one word after a place name: the whole area around or belonging to that place
with nothing left out; {tom kimcing} is brief but complete, and {a kimcing takin} is completely, in full
<gen> and <khial>, wrongly, written as one word: tell something incorrectly
the people of the <Hauzel> clan
<koppih>, partner, with the plural <te>
<saptuam>, church, with the plural <te>
<adem> and <ding> written as one word: the one who is to compete, as for an office or a seat

terms: every time it comes/whenever one arrives
definition: <tun>, arrive, and <sim>, every, written as one word: each time someone arrives or a time or event comes round

terms: even end up/go so far as
definition: <lawh>, as a result, and <liang>, even, written as one word after a verb: something goes so far that this is the outcome
<kha>, month, and <li>, four, written as one word
<an>, food, <sai.3>, shop, and the plural <te> written as one word: places where meals are sold and eaten
<khau>, rope, and <mong>, end, written as one word; also said in a figure of the one who holds the rope of a life
<toto>, more and more, with the plural <te>, after a verb: the people or things that keep on doing or being so
<ciang>, when or up to, and the particle <bel> written as one word: only at that time or point, at last by then

terms: for the length of/for a period of
definition: <sung>, during, and <ding> written as one word after a length of time: for that long; in a few sentences it is another {sung ding}, to be put in
<tel>, understand, with <sut.2>, untie: take a matter apart in order to understand it; {kampau telsut} is given for linguistics
<sing>, tree, with <sawl.3>, leafy branch: a branch of a tree, also cut branches used as cover
<khamuan>, peace of mind, with <huai>: giving confidence and ease of mind, said of news, plans and leaders

terms: let us at once/let us right away
definition: <pah>, at once, and <ni>, let us, written as one word after a verb: let us do it straight away
<a> and <kihuan> written as one word: it is cooked, or the thing that is cooked
<khut>, hand, with <suak.3>, come out: what the hands of someone have made, a work or product, and of God his creation
older, Lusei name for the Mara people of southern Mizoram and the neighbouring Chin Hills, and for their language
a hundred years, after <kum> and often with a number, {kum zabi 19} is the 19th century; the Mizo word, used by some writers where others write <zalom>
the wish to be well known or praised, named among faults such as selfishness and pride

terms: this way and that/again and again
definition: sound word placed after a verb, the action goes on or is repeated, {kawi kaihkaih} is twist this way and that, of words not speak straight
love and longing for the homeland; {gamngaihna la} is a patriotic song
the work that follows the burning of a hill field, when the wood left unburnt is gathered into heaps before sowing
the meat of the wild boar, <ngal> with <sa.1>
<guang> doubled, put things into a bag, box or other holder one after another
<mahmah> and <loh> written as one word after a verb, mostly <theih>, really not, not at all; {theih mahmahloh} is what cannot be done or is not known at all
{mop}, give from the mouth into the mouth of another, with <ki>, of drink, breath or words being given so; {thu kimop} is advice fed to someone
<khatkhat> and <ah> written as one word; {mun khatkhatah} is in some places
<khat> with <ten.2>, the plural marker joined with the marker of the doer, written as one word; {pawl khatten} is some people, as the ones who act
<nul> and <siang> written as one word, wipe something until it is clean or dry, as feet, tears or the top of a tin
sound word placed after a verb or describing word, covered or coloured all over, as with dust, grey fur or a blanket
the pot in which food, <an>, is cooked, <an> with <beel>; {anbeel suang} is put the pot on the fire
sound word placed after a verb of working or going, the action moves on quickly and without stopping

terms: be able to learn/manage to study
definition: <sin> and <zo> written as one word, <zo> here be able to, manage to learn or study
placed after a word or phrase to stress it, even that, that too, all the more; found in the articles of one writer and perhaps related to <semsem>

terms: be cleared clean/be cleaned up/clean up
definition: <kihah.3> and <siang> written as one word, of a house, a village or the ground round something, be cleared and cleaned; of people, clean up
<et> and <cim.2> written as one word, have looked enough; mostly with <lo> or {thei lo}, never tire of looking, of something beautiful
<tuah> and <loh> written as one word, not coming together; {kithu tuahloh} is disagreement
<zawl.4>, lover, with <gai>, being with child by a lover and not by a husband, or the woman who is so; held a great disgrace in former times
closes a clause that gives a known fact as the reason for what follows, since it is so, after all
a creature of Zomi folk tales, a kind of tiger or beast with magic power that can take the form of a person, known from the tale of {Vanleng Tanu}
<thau.3> and <lawn.3> written as one word, fire guns into the air, as men do at a feast, over big game and at a funeral

terms: share a meal with/treat to a meal
definition: after <ankuang>, sit round the dish with someone, invite a person to a meal or eat it together with him; the verb of {ankuang um}, sit round the dish, with the ending <pih.1>
<lung>, heart, with <kituak.1>, agreeing with one another in heart and mind; {lungkituak takin} is in unity
the sound of laughter, written alone or after <nui>, laugh; a shorter <hahaha>
<a> and <zumhuai> written as one word, it is shameful, the shameful thing
<hum>, shield, with <tuam>, separately, protect or favour one person apart from the rest; as a noun paired with <paihtuam>, {humtuam paihtuam} is favouritism and partiality
sound word placed after a verb, of laughing aloud, a fire blazing up or water bubbling, with noise and force
<tawmtawm> and <in> written as one word, a little at a time
the hornbill of the Zo country, the great hornbill, <Vaphual>; the pattern of the Zomi cloth is taken from it
<si> and <lah.2> written as one word, used before <nungta>, {silah nungta} is dead and yet living, alive but as good as dead
<lim>, form, and <lian> written as one word, in songs of a mithun or an elephant, large and fine of form
the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia, called by the short form of its Malay name
<koh.1> and <ni> written as one word after <lungdam>, {lungdam kohni} is Thanksgiving Day, the day of giving thanks
<Vaigam> with the ending <a.4> written as one word, in India or of India; {Kawlgam Vaigama Zomite} is the Zomi of Burma and India
<hi> and <manin> written as one word after <ka>, <i> or <tua>, because I am, because we are, that being so; the same as <hihmanin>

terms: way of being rich/how to be rich
definition: <hauh> and <dan> written as one word: the way of being or becoming rich, how wealth is gained and handled
<a> and <kimanna> written as one word: the use or value of it, {akimanna om lo} is it is of no use
<a> and <pii> written as one word, the verb lead or bring a person along: he or she brings someone along
<a> and <pii> written as one word: the female or mother of an animal, set beside <atal>, the male; also said of a grandmother

terms: whatever one wants/all that one likes/as one pleases
definition: <ut> and <teng> written as one word: all that someone wants, or all those who want to; {a utteng} is whatever he or she likes
placed after a describing word: a rather or fairly great degree of it, as {a sawt simkhat}, quite a long while
<kek>, widen, with the noun suffix <na>: the widening or extending of land or territory, as {gam kekna}; {kigi kekna} is the pushing out of a boundary
<i> and <ngahna> written as one word: the getting of something by us, or the way we got it
the bringing of a meeting, a tournament or a course to its end, and the ceremony held for it, from <hial>, conclude; {mahialna nei} is hold the closing
a city in the state of Texas in the United States, where a Zomi community lives
respect or honour shown to a person, as {zahna pia}, pay respect; the same as <zahtakna>
of the Mongol peoples; in Zolai writing the race of East Asia to which the Zomi are counted, as {Mongolian minam}
a city in the state of Assam in north-east India
<a> and <keem> written as one word: he or she keeps or looks after, or the one who looks after a child, a person or a thing
<i> and <cihna> written as one word: what we call a thing, or what we mean by saying it
an island country in the Indian Ocean, lying low above the sea
a place in the Tedim area of Chin State, with a stream of the same name; written small, {suangkua} is a cave in rock, and the word also names a thorny flowering tree
<min> and <teng> written as one word: all the names, or all the people who are named, as {anuai a minteng}, all those named below
<phi> and <khit> written as one word: having sat an interview or a test, {phikhit zawh} is after having sat it
<a> and <tuuk> written as one word: the autumn or harvest season; elsewhere the verb <tuuk>, he or she falls
said of a shirt or jacket with short sleeves, set beside <bansau>, long-sleeved
a story of love between two people, the English word written as one; the Zolai for it is <zawlthu>
<mi> and <muanhuai> written as one word: a person who can be trusted
regular and steady, as it should be; after <nisim> or {ni sim} it means regularly, and {pongmaan lo} is not proper, not in order
<bei> and <a> written as one word, after an amount of money, time or strength: with that much used up, at that cost
<peem>, migrate, with the prefix {ki-}: of people, move away from the home place and settle elsewhere; {kipem khia} is migrate out

terms: we take part/we are included/we are among
definition: <i> and <kihel> written as one word: we take part in something or are counted among a group
<min> and <tuam> written as one word: a name of its own, apart from the common name, as each group or association takes one
<a> and <tawh> written as one word: with, together with, where the prefix is joined to the postposition; in one sentence it is {a tawh}, his key
<hong> and <gah> written as one word: bear fruit, said of a plant and of work or ideas that come to a result
<hi>, be, with the particle <saam>: be so indeed or be no more than that; {hisaam taleh} is even though it is, and {hisaam lo} or {hisaam kei} is it is not just that
<hong> and <that> written as one word: kill, with the action turned toward the speaker or told as an event
<nencip>, press down, with the noun suffix <na>: the bearing down on people by those with power; {nencipna thuak} is suffer oppression
the state of having an equal share or standing; {numei leh pasal tankimna} is equality of women and men
<gualtung> and <tuanna> written as one word: the rising above one's peers, success or the upper hand
<nei> and <lua> written as one word: have too much or very much of something
meat of game or other animals dried or smoked in strips so that it keeps, stored in baskets and brought as a gift
<tektek> and <ah> written as one word, after a noun of place: right at that very place, as {ka muhna tektekah}, right before my eyes
the state of falling short or not being enough, a shortcoming of a person, set beside <thanemna>, weakness
<thusim> and <loh> written as one word: not paying regard to a person, the form of <thusimlo> used before a noun or as a noun
a city in the state of Maryland in the United States, near Washington, where Zomi families live
<zi>, wife, <leh>, and, and <ta>, child, written as one word: a man's wife and children
<nekpih>, eat with someone, with the prefix <ki>: people eat or drink something together with one another
<deih>, like, with <tuam>, apart: liked above the others, one's own particular choice; {deihtuam nei} is have a special preference, be selective
<min>, name, with <saanna>, here acceptance: the entering of a person's name on a list as a member, or as a refugee with the UN
<paina>, going, with the plural <te>: the journeys or visits someone makes, the places gone to; before <in> also those who went
<lam>, build, with <toh>, upward: build something up, as a road, a church, a country or the future
<huansung>, the inside of a garden, and the place marker <ah> written as one word: in the garden
<piak>, give, with <thuah>, in addition: give something more on top of what is given; of money, pay extra
<mawk>, without care or purpose, and <pai>, go, written as one word: go to a place when there is no need or without thinking

terms: help one another carry/share burdens/bear together
definition: <puakpih>, help carry, with the prefix <ki>: people help one another carry a load or bear a burden or a cost

terms: be good at once/get well quickly/be fine
definition: <hoih>, good, with <pah>, at once: become good or well straight away; with <sa> or <lel> after it, find a thing simply good or fitting
<hah>, clean, and <ding>, to, written as one word: to clean a place or a thing, what is to be cleaned
<ngak>, wait, with <phot>, first: wait for something before doing anything else
<i>, our, and <lawm>, friend, written as one word

terms: right upon/from the very/on that same
definition: <tung>, on or from a person or thing, with the emphatic <mah> written as one word: on or from that very one, often followed by <pan> or <ah>
<bucing>, complete, with the causative <sak>: make a thing whole so that nothing is lacking, fulfil

terms: those who just do/those who do outright
definition: the adverb <giapgiap>, firmly and without holding back, with the plural <te>, after a verb: the people who simply do the thing straight out
<kipawl>, associate or band together, with <zia>, manner: how people keep company or how a group is organised

terms: as it says/as the saying goes/as he says
definition: <acih>, what is said, and <bang>, like, written as one word: as he said, in keeping with the words just quoted
<khuakpil>, intelligent, with the noun suffix {-na}: the power of the brain to learn and think
<tan>, here shine, said of the sun and the moon, with <lai>, while: at the time when the sun or the moon is shining

terms: when it arrives/when he reaches/when it comes
definition: <atun>, he or it arrives, and <teh>, when, written as one word: when a person reaches a place or a time comes
<a> and <kine>, be eaten, written as one word: that which is eaten, it is eaten; {akine thei} is edible

terms: to hear/for hearing/what is to be heard
definition: <zak>, hear, and <ding>, to, written as one word: for someone to hear, what should be heard
<nuntak>, live, and <khuasakna>, way of life, written as one word: a person's life and the way it is lived and earned
<mangpha>, goodbye, with <khakna>, sending: the saying of farewell, in notices the last tribute paid to a person who has died, as with a wreath; also a farewell message
the particle <kha>, happen to, and <den>, always, written as one word after a verb: the thing keeps on happening or being done
<na>, you, and <sakte>, those considered, written as one word after a describing word: the people or things that you find to be so
word of songs, apparently a tree whose leaf, {thel nah}, stands for a letter or a sheet of paper, <thelnah>; {thel bang} is like the thel
<ka>, I, and <zuih>, follow, written as one word: I follow, what I am to follow
<bawng>, ox, with <leng>, cart: a cart drawn by oxen
<sem>, work, with <ten>, the plural <te> joined with the doer marker <in>: those who do the work named before it, as the doers of the action; more carefully written {semte'n}
go past a thing without stopping at it: leave a matter aside for the time being, or get over a barrier that divides
the Passover of the Bible, written with a capital: {Paikan Belamno} is the Passover lamb
<lem>, be suitable, with <sa>, consider: find a thing fitting and so allow it; often of God, {Pasian in lemsa}, God wills or permits it
a blessing, used in hymns and church writing beside <thupha>; {vualzawl} is bless
placed after a verb for an action done quickly and repeatedly, as wiping, greeting or setting off
found in writing from Manipur in Paite style: at the present time, where Tedim writes {tu laitak}
<tan.2>, up to, and <a> written as one word after a word of time, as {tuni tana}, up to today, to this day; the same letters also end the unrelated {piah-tana}
the matters of the evening, in the pair {zingvai nitakvai}, the morning and evening affairs: the daily running of a household or a people, which one manages, <hawm>
<ginatlohna> with the plural <te>: the ways in which a person is not as he should be
<Suangthu> and <thum> written as one word: the three stones of the hearth that carry the pot, said of three bodies that together bear one whole
<Teizang> with the plural <te>: the people of the Teizang group among the Zomi, with their own way of speaking
<a> and <cinuam> written as one word: want to say, what one means; {acinuam ka hihi} is that is what I mean
in the pair {gamnu gampa}, the women and men of a country, said of the children who will be its citizens and leaders
<sihsak> with the ending {-na}: the act of causing death, also death as the sentence of a court
<vet> and <in> written as one word after a verb: at all, even so much as, altogether
the great river of China, counted the longest river of Asia
<khuak> with the plural <te>: the brain as the seat of thinking and memory
placed after a verb: do the thing straight off, without holding back or thinking it over
<i> and <suak> written as one word: we become, we turn out to be

terms: what we already know/as we know
definition: <i> and <theihsa> written as one word: a thing that we already know
the sea that Israel crossed on dry ground when leaving Egypt
<himawh> and <in> written as one word, after <lung>: being worried or concerned about something

terms: be able to talk together/be on speaking terms
definition: <kiho> and <theih> written as one word: be able to speak with each other, be on good terms
the worship of spirits, <dawi>, the old religion before Christianity; {dawibiak hun} is the time of spirit worship
<bang> and <gen> written as one word in a question: what does one say
<mai> with the plural <te>: the fronts of houses, shops and offices
<Mimbung>, a village in Mizoram, with <ah>, at or to, written as one word: at Mimbung
<laihsak> and <ding> written as one word: will change one thing for another
<a> and <khuasuak> written as one word: he or it succeeds, the one who gets on in life
<innveng> with <pa>: a man who lives next door, a male neighbour
<a>, <khan> and <khiat> written as one word: he grows up, they grow up
redness of the eyes, named among the signs of an illness
<nasep> and <tawh> written as one word: with the work, as in {naseptawh kisai}, concerning the work
the minister who looks after a congregation, mostly as {pawlpi kemsia}, church pastor
<tam> and <pia> written as one word: give a large amount
what lies outside a church or group, the opposite of <pawlsung>; {pawlpua mi} is an outsider
the fellowship of Christians with one another, a term of church teaching mostly added beside the Zolai wording
<kihel> and <den> written as one word: take part every time
<va> and <tai> written as one word: go off running to a place, flee there
<min> and <peuh> written as one word: a name of whatever kind, after each of several names that are listed
capital city of Yemen

terms: want to go home/want to return
definition: <ciah> and <nuam> written as one word: want to go home or go back
plural of <pawldang>: the other groups or parties, in church matters the other denominations
<pia> and <zia> written as one word, the same as <piakzia>: the way something is given or granted
bring a speech, a writing or a matter to its close, sum it up; the noun is <thukhupna>

terms: be able to be complete/all be able
definition: <kim>, complete or all, and <thei>, able, written as one word: able to be complete or satisfied, or all able to be there
<teek>, old, with <sia> in the sense bad or worn: one who is old and worn out, the frail aged; a rough word that an article advises against using of elders
<ahang> and <khat> written as one word: one reason, a reason of some kind; with <peuhpeuh>, for whatever reason
<ka> and <nasep> written as one word: my work, my job or office
placed after a verb, mostly <thei>, know, of something known or true all along, usually before a clause that tells what is done in spite of it; compare <gige>
<ngiat> and <a> written as one word: specially, on purpose, after <ding> or <ading> made expressly for; after a describing word, really
city in France; also met as a family name and in names of companies
<sim> and <lai> written as one word: still reading or studying, while studying, in a command read once more; with <sim> in its sense attack, while attacking
city in the north of India, seat of the institute of technology IIT Kanpur
village in Mizoram on the Tlawng river, near Aizawl
ending of a sentence in quoted everyday speech, mostly as {aita ve}, apparently a spoken short form of {ahi ta}: so it is, it seems, and in a question, is it then
<bul>, base, with <pat>, begin: begin at the root or source, start from the very beginning
<kikhek>, be changed, with the causative <sak>: make something change, or be changed into something different

terms: try to master/strive to be good at
definition: <siam>, skilled, and <sawm>, intend, written as one word: set out to become good at something, often paired with <theihsawm>, try to know
plural of <thuciin>: the sayings and teachings handed down, also the principles that something rests on
{na'ng uh}, the short form of {nading uh}, written as one word after a verb: for them to do it, so that they may
the rope or strap with which a load is tied and carried on the back
<ni>, sun, with <liap>, be shaded: the shade, a place the sun does not reach, as under a house or a tree
<hilh> and <thei> written as one word: able to teach or to explain
<kem> and <lai> written as one word: still keeping, still have in one's care
<a> and <taangzai> written as one word: wide, broad in reach or outlook, that which is wide
expressive word placed after words of shining and of redness, such as <taang> and <san>: bright and glowing, of sunshine, a deep red colour or reddened eyes
<hun>, time, with <pat>, begin: the beginning of a season or the opening of a meeting or programme, as in {hunpat thungetna}, opening prayer; also as a verb, open the programme
<asaang> and <zaw> written as one word: higher, that which is higher, in place, level or standing

terms: feel at home/be at ease/be settled in
definition: be familiar and comfortable in the place where one is, at home there; also said of a guest who behaves like the owner of the house
<a> and <lemtaang> written as one word: convenient, going well, that which is convenient
